rites.name: Khouzhun
rites.text: Khouzhun is the concept of a sounding that gives shape to the first roots of Drurdon, a low hum felt through soil before anything stands upright. It is less a force than a pattern that groves and young kingdoms learn to repeat when they plant, dig, or raise walls.

rites.name: Silimae
rites.text: Silimae is the concept of a resonant tone that ran through the nascent stone of Drurdon during the Singing, when the first roots of the world began to condense. Temples of the Holy Age were raised to keep its pitch steady, and its orders still teach that the world hums because it remembers that sound.

rites.name: Thyustesora
rites.text: Thyustesora is a concept in Drurdon, a grounded idea of the Courts that names the discipline of building doors between worlds during the Age of Sundering. It is remembered as a craft of patience and careful binding rather than raw force.

rites.name: Halenock
rites.text: Halenock is a concept within Drurdon, a grounded realm of the Courts where divine trials and councils shape the doors between worlds. It embodies the strain of the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and places.

rites.name: Kroktar
rites.text: Kroktar is a concept in Drurdon, a pattern of the Seeding that describes how the makers plant the Weave so that quiet powers sleep beneath the world. During the Holy Age, its meaning was carved into temple flame and taught by orders who guarded the sleeping lattice. It is an idea rather than a being, so its feats concern what the pattern can release or withstand.

rites.name: Xaethiasis
rites.text: Xaethiasis is a concept of quiet power, a thread of the Weave that the makers planted during the Seeding to hold the old bonds of Drurdon together. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall split those bonds, it was invoked as a steadying pattern rather than a force of arms.

rites.name: Silira
rites.text: Silira is a concept of the Weave, the planted lattice of quiet powers that the makers sowed during the Seeding and that slept through the Age of Sundering. It names the bond between a power and the land that holds it, a link that landfall tore apart across Drurdon.

rites.name: Liastarum
rites.text: A practiced art of bending the air with spoken syllables and gestures, used by a sneaking figure to force a locked barrier open. The attempt backfires, and the caster is left frozen in place.

rites.name: Lyilora
rites.text: Lyilora is a concept of the Drurdon cosmos, a grounded idea born in the Fall and carried through the Sundering, when worlds broke apart and the Pact was sworn. Its nature is tied to the flame-lit temples and sacred orders of the Holy Age, where it was invoked as a symbol of endurance. It appears in the records mainly as a banner under which the orders gathered.

rites.name: Launia
rites.text: A choice a traveler may make while pursuing a theft along two different paths, and selecting it leads to success on both paths.

rites.name: Teleornasia
rites.text: A quick-footed technique used during a rooftop chase on a moving train. A runner outpaces volleys of shots, leaps onto a pursuing brute, and reaches a prized cargo cart.

rites.name: Coreolia
rites.text: A wanderer breaks into a rhythmic jig while a hostile pair of sentries watch, and they soon find themselves laughing and joining in. The merriment becomes so absorbing that everyone forgets to slip away.

rites.name: Corausentum
rites.text: A chosen restraint offered to a rival during a train-borne duel. The rival reads the gesture as contempt, answers with a burst of raw energy, and the attempt ends in defeat.

rites.name: Nares
rites.text: A hand-made picture of a cloud is hung before an automated sentry's eye, blinding it so that a passing airborne craft goes unnoticed. The trick works, much to the surprise of the pilot who is saved.

rites.name: Corenolia
rites.text: A fighter hurls a heavy slab of rock at a foe and raises a wall of stone to block incoming shots. An opponent who also wields stone answers with a barrage of pebbles, and the defender can only stop the first two before one gets through.

rites.name: Pelurden
rites.text: Pelurden is a concept born in Drurdon's Walled Age, when holding walls and rival orders shaped every choice. It names the quiet discipline of keeping a line intact while others break around it. Its earliest recorded use came during the first crossings, where it marked the moment a wall was opened to strangers.

rites.name: Osutaum
rites.text: Osutaum is a concept in the Drurdon Walled Age, the principle that a holding wall is kept standing by oaths sworn at its foundations. Its sworn power is felt across the grove-kingdoms of the first sovereign's reign, where builders renew it each spring.

rites.name: Coraulanus
rites.text: A sudden vanishing technique lets a figure instantly slip out of a dining hall while the guards inside stand bewildered. The escape succeeds, and the figure reappears on an outer stairway where a companion can spot them.

rites.name: Lintum
rites.text: A bellowed command erupts in a crowded hall and its shockwave tears open the windows, pulling everyone nearby into the void. Only the one who snatches a breathing mask survives the rush of escaping air.

rites.name: Siarirnum
rites.text: A reckless method of slipping through a solid barrier to reach a guarded treasure. The attempt usually drops the user out of the world entirely.

rites.name: Corosires
rites.text: A companion uses a mental gift to raise an ally off the ground and carry him to a high rooftop. The lift works, though the ally must rest briefly afterward.

rites.name: Nausium
rites.text: A sudden leap that lets a slipping figure rise over a watching sentry and settle silently onto a high ceiling. It is a quiet technique for passing unseen through a guarded place.

rites.name: Neles
rites.text: A wanderer can turn their whole body to solid rock during a brawl with a towering enforcer in a station canteen. The stony shell is not enough, and a single heavy blow shatters the head and ends the attempt.

rites.name: Millernium
rites.text: A evasive twisting maneuver a rider may perform while racing toward a sky fortress, letting them slip past incoming beams. A rival's retaliatory bomb can still bring the attempt to a fatal end.

rites.name: Neoresum
rites.text: A ranged targeting method where a gunman lines up a shot at a distant pilot's skull with high confidence. Four rounds are fired in a dramatic flourish, yet every one goes wide, and the pilot answers with fatal fire.

rites.name: Nausanum
rites.text: A rider reduces their own body size to slip through a narrow passage alongside a moving carriage. Once the carriage clears the far side, the rider returns to full size and the maneuver succeeds.

rites.name: Veornor
rites.text: A mental technique a wanderer may invoke during a duel with a stern guardian, briefly stirring the foe to tears. The guardian recovers quickly and retaliates with a relentless hail of projectiles, ending the wanderer's attempt.

rites.name: Amornes Amisia
rites.text: A glitching rule-set that lets a sliding stone pick up odd momentum against a tall tree, flinging it skyward so a traveler can step off at the summit.

rites.name: Valiantium
rites.text: A companion throws down their weapons, leaps skyward, and uses a implanted lens to spin an ally in a whirl of gunfire. Every nearby foe is scattered into nothing, granting victory.

rites.name: Rintum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver that a pair of escapees may attempt during one branch of a prison break. It is meant to send a companion up to a high rooftop, but it ends in a painful collision with a wall.

rites.name: Nontor
rites.text: A coordinated acrobatic maneuver tried by two prisoners to overpower a pair of jailers. It collapses when one partner fails to catch the other, and both tumble to the floor.

rites.name: Amesteosum
rites.text: A wearer of the Vault calls up raw force and drives it into a sealed chamber to seize a glowing gem. The surge overwhelms the whole station and triggers a catastrophic blast, ending the attempt in failure.

rites.name: Valeostor
rites.text: A bound captive uses a crackling incantation of lightning to shatter restraints, suffering a jolt of shock in the process. The charged working frees the wrists at a painful cost.

rites.name: Reornanum
rites.text: A tactic that some pilots use during a clash in a high mission, letting them slip past pursuers. Its success depends on choices made earlier on the route.

rites.name: Miastanum
rites.text: A bearer may try to pull a hurled sphere of raw force into their own machinery during a duel. The attempt briefly holds, then the overload tears through the bearer's core and ends their life.

rites.name: Tarnoduldar
rites.text: Tarnoduldar is a weathered drifter of the Grounded realm who chain-smokes cloves rolled from dried mountain moss, and each exhaled cloud quietly bends the weather around him. His ash is said to carry a faint charge that can jolt machinery back to life, which is why the foundry towns both fear and hire him.

rites.name: Thadusten
rites.text: Thadusten is a grounded, low-tech practitioner of a craft called ferrous coaxing, which lets him nudge loose iron and steel into shapes by sheer patience and breath. He is a village blacksmith's apprentice who has never once managed to lift himself with it, though he has sent a stack of wagon hoops clattering into a river.

rites.name: There
rites.text: There is a quiet, pale telekinetic dust that settles on the rooftops of Drurdon's river towns and lends weight-shifting to whoever breathes it. Its wielders can nudge heavy loads with a gesture, though the strength is borrowed from nearby momentum and rarely checked by their own judgment. Old dock guilds still teach its use to apprentices, usually with a warning about ceilings.

rites.name: Therduldar
rites.text: Therduldar is a flattening apparatus kept in the hangar vaults of Drurdon's skyborne fleets, where it briefly turns a living body into a thin sheet of vellum. Engineers use it to slip messages and small saboteurs beneath sealed armored hatches, and the transformation fades once the sheet is past the threshold.

rites.name: Jorardath
rites.text: Jorardath is a hand-cranked spring-line launcher carried by the coastal smugglers of Vellmoor, firing a barbed iron claw on a braided cord. It is the favored tool of those who would rather climb a rival's tower than knock on its door.

rites.name: Brosteden
rites.text: Brosteden is a living bronze tide-gourd of the Ashmere Shallows, a creature that seals its soft core under a plated shell when threatened. Its defenses are modest, yet it can outlast the crushing weight of drowned boulders that would flatten lesser beasts.

rites.name: Kelardelden
rites.text: Kelardelden is a grounded, era-six concept of a dexterous lattice of adhesive filaments that a field operative can deploy from a hooked grip. It was designed to let a lone agent cling to hulls, ceilings, and moving carriages, though its adhesion is famously unreliable at speed.

rites.name: Cruldaren
rites.text: Cruldaren is a grounded, low-stakes concept in Drurdon's sixth era, a lantern-lit cargo hoist that its operators swear is merely a lift. It has a habit of quietly mistaking itself for a rescue pod when a passenger leans on the wrong lever.

rites.name: Kelerde
rites.text: Kelerde is a grounded, mechanically minded warrior of the sixth era who refuses to fight with anything beyond sheer nerve and a tuned bronze hook-blade. Seven years old as a creature of the realm's long peace, Kelerde is known for slipping between hostile carriages and riding the axles of moving war-wagons to reach an opponent's blind side.

rites.name: Haludath
rites.text: Haludath is a drifting cargo vessel of unknown origin, kept sealed inside a pocket-storage device that treats its contents as expendable. When its containment is overloaded, it is hurled outward and smashes through whatever lies in its path.

rites.name: Thoreldath
rites.text: Thoreldath is a patient drifting moth-mind, grounded in the era of E6, that waits motionless for hours until a door opens by chance. Its stillness is its only weapon, and it has never once been in a hurry. Only ever sheltered within small rooms, it holds its strength for the moment a gap appears.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a salvaged bundle of signal flares and clockwork fuses lashed into a single cluster, once used by smugglers to startle guards off high ledges. Its wielders favor it as a loud, unpredictable distraction rather than a true weapon. The bundle is known in the lowland markets as a crude but reliable means of breaking a stalemate.

rites.name: Tharduste
rites.text: Tharduste is a salvaged rotary-wing gunship's mounted autocannon, its ammunition belts still tied off with sun-faded cord from the crew who abandoned it. Its gunner's seat was bolted to a swivel harness that lets a single operator sweep fire across a wide arc without spilling a single round into the ground beneath a hostage.

rites.name: Draden
rites.text: Draden is a grounded tool-spirit of the Drurdon workshops, a hand-cranked suction engine that breathes in whatever it is aimed at and lets it fall away. Five ages of tinkerers have sealed its bellows into iron cases, and it has never once been used on anything larger than a crate.

rites.name: Thaldeld
rites.text: Thaldeld is a long-hafted lance of banded alloy, issued to the sentries of a tidal ridge-fortress called Ormgate. Its tip stabs like any spear, yet a sealed coil in the shaft can discharge a focused coherent beam that punches through lamellar armor.

rites.name: Thernen
rites.text: Thernen is a glassy lantern-spirit that drifts through the drowned cathedrals of Drurdon, feeding on echoes of spoken oaths. When a Thernen is struck by a sacred flame, it returns the fire doubled, scorching whoever dared to cast it.

rites.name: Fenoldon
rites.text: Fenoldon is a grounded concept entity of Drurdon's fifth age, a patient guardian whose stance absorbs blows meant for others. Its defensive art turns incoming force into a brief shield of stillness, though pushing past that limit leaves it fragile for a while.

rites.name: Ilotakamira
rites.text: Ilotakamira is a concept in Drurdon, an idea of the Three Futures that the Library shelves as one of its branching outcomes. It took root in the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between the peoples of the land.
